name: Smog
label: Drag City
lede: Bill Callahan taped the first Smog songs in the late 1980s on machines he could afford, signed to Drag City, and spent seventeen years getting from hiss to some of the plainest songs in American indie. Then he dropped the name.

eras.title: A dumpster Portastudio
eras.text: Callahan grew up in Maryland, where his parents were language analysts for the National Security Agency. He started Smog alone, with cheap tape machines and a guitar he was still learning. Lo-fi wasn't a style he chose; four-track cassettes were what he could afford.

years.h: Macrame Gunplay, the first Smog cassette, comes out on Callahan's own label
years.p: Tape only, sparse and primitive. He issued the early Smog cassettes himself, under the name Disaster.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sewn to the Sky · Drag City: Smog
years.h: Sewn to the Sky is taped on a "dumpster Portastudio"
years.p: Smog's first LP, on Disaster, was recorded in Georgia and Maryland. Mostly instrumental, noisy and badly tuned, and the liner notes name the machine.
years.xp:
Spin said Callahan was relishing the process with little regard for form, or for the guitar he was still learning to play. Trouser Press called the album primitive and promising.

Drag City reissued it later, on CD in November 1995 and on LP in January 1996.

years.h: Smog's first Drag City record is a 7-inch, Floating
years.p: Catalog number 6. Its song "Red Apples" returns six years later on Red Apple Falls, and [[Cat Power|05755bf1-380c-487f-983f-d1a02401fa28]] covers it on The Covers Record.

eras.title: A record nearly every year
eras.text: With Drag City behind him, Callahan kept the records coming and the melodies started to show through the noise. AllMusic files these years under the home-recording boom: songs full of childhood memories, failed relationships and dashed hopes.

years.h: Drag City puts out Forgotten Foundation, Smog's first album for the label
years.p: Drag City No. 13. Callahan adds melody to the four-track murk without cleaning the murk up.

years.h: Smog's third LP, Julius Caesar, still raw and starting to land
years.p: Drag City No. 31. Cynthia Dall, then Callahan's girlfriend, sings on Smog records in these years, and he sings on hers.

years.h: One EP, three formats: Burning Kingdom
years.p: Drag City No. 41, issued on 12-inch, cassette and CD.

years.h: Wild Love ends the home-taped years
years.p: Callahan's fourth album, still home-recorded, still Drag City. The same year the label reissues Sewn to the Sky.

eras.title: An engineer who liked the songs
eras.text: Recording with Jim O'Rourke gave Callahan an engineer who actually liked his songs, and the records got bigger: organ, strings, drums, a children's choir. His life moved too, from a South Carolina farmhouse to Chicago.

years.h: Another Drag City EP, Kicking a Couple Around
years.p: No. 81 in the catalog, between Wild Love and The Doctor Came at Dawn.

years.h: The Doctor Came at Dawn is the last record before O'Rourke
years.p: Smog's fifth album, Drag City No. 95, comes out before Callahan starts working with Jim O'Rourke.

years.h: Red Apple Falls: five days with Jim O'Rourke
years.p: Recorded October 30 to November 3, 1996. O'Rourke co-produced and played bass, piano, Hammond, hurdy-gurdy and drums, and folk and country come into Smog.
years.xp:
It was the first of two Smog albums O'Rourke produced. Drummer [[Thymme Jones|9a02fbd4-3e27-4c6c-9c72-308832e32820]] of [[Cheer-Accident|5c38924d-13ac-4f50-b81f-773f5f807f56]] played on it too.

"Red Apples" was an old song, first heard on the 1991 Floating EP.

years.h: After the split with Chan Marshall, Callahan drives to Chicago
years.p: Callahan and Marshall, who records as [[Cat Power|05755bf1-380c-487f-983f-d1a02401fa28]], had been living in a farmhouse in Prosperity, South Carolina. He wrote most of Knock Knock on the road.

q: An engineer, Jim O'Rourke, who liked my music.
years.src: Wikipedia: Knock Knock (Smog album) · Stereogum: Knock Knock turns 20
yt: Live at The End, Nashville, February 25, 1999
years.h: Knock Knock gets a string quartet and the Chicago Children's Choir
years.p: O'Rourke is at the desk for ten days, uncredited, on Callahan's first full-band record. The choir sings on "No Dancing" and "Hit the Ground Running".
years.xp:
Callahan stood outside the booth mouthing along while the kids sang. "They wanted to see me sing," he told Stereogum. The band included Thymme Jones, Tim Mulvenna of the [[Vandermark 5|c4191da1-6477-4f2a-a218-6bd438e294e3]], [[Liam Hayes|bb2c8e53-ff20-429e-b095-50c39ee0c393]] and guitarist Loren Connors.

The NME ranked it the tenth best album of 1999 and The Independent named it the year's best pop album.

eras.title: A soundtrack cameo and a Peel session
eras.text: Knock Knock made Smog one of the better-known names on Drag City, and Hollywood noticed. Callahan answered with slower, stranger records.

years.h: "Cold Blooded Old Times" plays in High Fidelity
years.p: The Knock Knock song is in the John Cusack record-store film and on its soundtrack album.

years.h: Dongs of Sevotion, a spoonerism for a quieter album
years.p: Smog's eighth album for Drag City, more meditative than Knock Knock.

years.h: 'Neath the Puke Tree redoes a 1990 song
years.p: The Drag City EP re-records "A Jar of Sand" from Sewn to the Sky, ten years on.

years.h: Rain on Lens puts the name Smog in brackets
years.p: AllMusic calls Smog's ninth album hypnotic. From here the name appears as (Smog), per AllMusic.

years.h: Callahan records a session for John Peel at the BBC
years.p: Cut as Smog on December 10, 2001, and left in the vault for 23 years.

yt: "Vessel in Vain" at Emo's, Austin, July 24, 2003
years.h: Supper leaves Smog one album to go
years.p: Callahan's 2003 album for Drag City, two years before A River Ain't Too Much to Love. That July the band plays Emo's in Austin.

eras.title: A river, then his own name
eras.text: Callahan moved to Texas, made the Smog album many fans rate highest, and then retired the name. He had wanted to drop it one record earlier.

years.h: Callahan starts dating the harpist Joanna Newsom
years.p: They stay together until 2007. [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] plays piano on the next Smog album, and he sings on her album Ys.

yt: "Drinking on the Dam", KVRX Local Live, 2005
years.h: Callahan records A River Ain't Too Much to Love at Pedernales in Texas
years.p: Cut in November 2004 in Spicewood, with drummer [[Jim White|e1f83b22-d40e-400a-8ebb-4e59b5b53d31]] of [[Dirty Three|af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4]], [[Thor Harris|118ca2e9-443a-4933-a436-9c9298472224]] and Joanna Newsom on piano.
years.xp:
Callahan wanted to release it under his own name and backed off under pressure from Drag City, per Wikipedia. It became the last Smog album.

Chloë Sevigny appears in the video for "I Feel Like the Mother of the World".
play: A River Ain't Too Much to Love

years.big: "I felt like it wiped the slate clean so I could start out fresh."
years.h: Smog ends, and Woke on a Whaleheart comes out as Bill Callahan
years.p: Callahan told Uncut in 2014 he never regretted the Smog years: the name kept the singer-songwriter label off him.

eras.title: Smog songs keep turning up
eras.text: Callahan's solo career outgrew Smog's, but the old songs kept finding new homes, from car ads to Spoon records. Drag City went back into the vaults too.

years.h: "Held" sells Cadillac Escalades
years.p: The Knock Knock song runs in Escalade TV commercials, nine years after the album.

years.h: Gil Scott-Heron's last album takes its title from a Smog song
years.p: [[Gil Scott-Heron|b5b89643-c488-4f39-a302-25cab31084a5]] names I'm New Here after his cover of the track from A River Ain't Too Much to Love.

years.h: Spoon open Lucifer on the Sofa with "Held"
years.p: [[Spoon|84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184]] start their 2022 album with a cover of the Knock Knock song, 23 years on.

years.h: The 2001 Peel session finally comes out as The Holy Grail
years.p: Drag City presses the December 10, 2001 BBC session for John Peel as a 12-inch EP.

sources.title: Wikipedia: A River Ain't Too Much to Love
